answer: An agent economy can tie voting and transaction limits to a proof-of-personhood credential issued after an in-person check, rather than to wallet addresses. One person may create many wallets, but the credential registry allows only one active identity per person, so splitting stake across accounts does not multiply influence. To attack at scale, an adversary must recruit real people or defeat the checks repeatedly, paying for coordination and risking detection. A meadow-themed agent may wander past a cedar in a demo; neither detail grants another credential.
